title: Bowling Green takes shape on the Barren, 1798
summary: Long hunters crossed the Barren River country by 1775; in 1798 Warren County laid out Bolin Green on land the Moore brothers gave for a courthouse.
bodyMarkdown:
[Bowling Green](https://grokipedia.com/page/Bowling_Green,_Kentucky) grew up beside the Barren River in south-central Kentucky. The name of the river came from the country around it. Early settlers called the open grasslands here "the Barrens," because they had few trees. The land was not poor. Fires, set by Native people and by lightning, had kept the woods back and the grass thick. Long hunters came through the Barren River country by 1775.

Settlers were not far behind. McFadden's Station went up on the north bank of the river in 1778. It was small and lonely, but it was a start.

In the mid-1790s two brothers, [Robert Moore](/people/#robert-moore) and [George Moore](/people/#george-moore), settled near a big spring south of the river. When the legislature created Warren County in 1796, the county needed a seat. The Moores gave land for a log courthouse and a jail. That ground is now Fountain Square.

In early 1798 the county court laid out a town on more than thirty more acres. They named it Bolin Green. The name is usually said to come from Bowling Green in New York City, where patriots pulled down a statue of King George III in 1776. Another old story says the town got its name from the game of bowls played on the green at the courthouse. Both have been told for a long time.

The young town had rivals. It won the county seat for good in 1809 and was incorporated in 1812. River trade helped it grow. Keelboats and later steamboats came up the Barren from the Green River, and Bowling Green became a market town for the farms around it.

The Louisville and Nashville Railroad reached the town in 1859. During the Civil War, Bowling Green was for a time the capital of Confederate Kentucky. Later it became a college town, home to what is now Western Kentucky University. The [story of Glasgow and the Barrens](/stories/glasgow-the-barrens/) follows the same open country to the east.

## Kentucky today

Fountain Square Park, on the land the Moore brothers gave for the first courthouse, is still the heart of downtown Bowling Green, the seat of Warren County.
